subject: Evaluation lanecard & ephemeral assets — MAP and takedown timeline
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Chen <alice@novaretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation lanecard & ephemeral assets — MAP and takedown timeline

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I put together a lightweight MAP and a proposed lanecard for exchanging a small evaluation corpus and a prompt pack so your engineers can validate latency and behavioral regressions on a staging instance. The attached MAP_NovaRetail_v3.xlsx includes milestones; the two core items we’ll exchange are: the Nova eval dataset (sample subset) and the prompt pack (structured prompt + test cases).

High level proposal (please confirm):
- Access: ephemeral sandbox (tokenized) provisioned for 30 days.
- Assets: secure S3 transfer of Nova_eval_dataset_v1.zip + promptpack_v2.pdf; read-only access.
- Usage constraints: no redistribution, no model-training on the raw dataset outside the sandbox, downstream log retention limited to 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Acceptance gate: run the 120-case smoke suite from the prompt pack; pass rate >= 95% on behavior anchors + provide token-level latency stats.
- Takedown: assets removed and credentials revoked 14 days after the end of the evaluation window (or immediately on contract termination).

Proposed timeline (tentative):
1) 11/22 — Legal sign-off on MAP + NDA appendix (your side)
2) 11/24 — Redwood to provision ephemeral sandbox + upload assets
3) 11/25–12/24 — 30-day evaluation window (start when sandbox credentials issued)
4) 12/26 — Final acceptance report; if accepted, discuss next steps (pilot terms)

Can you confirm the constraints above or flag any must-haves (e.g., additional logging/Audit access or longer retention)? I copied Karthik and Priyom for the provisioning & ops bits, and Laura for contractual milestone alignment.

Attachments: MAP_NovaRetail_v3.xlsx, Nova_eval_dataset_v1.zip (index stub), promptpack_v2.pdf

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0132

From: Alice Chen <alice@novaretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novaretail.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation lanecard & ephemeral assets — MAP and takedown timeline

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear plan — this looks like a good starting point. A couple of asks from our side before we sign:

1) Can we add a clause that requires an audit log export (redacted) at the end of the evaluation so we can reconcile prompts used vs outputs?
2) We typically request a 45-day window for certain vertical tests (payment flow simulations). Can we make the window configurable, with a default of 30 and an option to extend to 45 with 7 days' notice?
3) Since the dataset contains PHI-simulated rows, our security team needs confirmation that Redwood’s ephemeral sandbox will not allow data egress and that all KV caches are flushed on takedown. Can you point us to a short ops note or checklist?

If you can agree to (1) and provide the ops checklist, I’ll route the MAP back to legal for a quick sign-off.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Senior ML Product Manager, NovaRetail
alice@novaretail.com | +1 617-555-0202

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
To: Alice Chen <alice@novaretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evaluation lanecard & ephemeral assets — MAP and takedown timeline

Alice —

Great questions. Short answers up front and details below.

- Audit export: yes — we can provide a redacted audit log export (CSV) covering request timestamps, route/model used, prompt hash (SHA256), and token counts. No raw outputs will be included unless you request them explicitly.
- Window flexibility: we can start with 30 days and provide a one-time extension to 45 days if requested 7 days before the scheduled end; we’ll reflect that in the MAP draft.
- Ops checklist / egress guarantees: attached is a short ops note (promptpack_v2.pdf includes a 1-page sandbox checklist). Key points: KV cache flush, prefix-only caching, no external network egress from sandbox, credentials revoked on takedown, and a tamper-evident audit trail.

Acceptance criteria refinements (updated):
- Smoke suite: 120 cases as-is; pass rate >=95% on behavior anchors.
- Latency target: median < 220ms token time for the scripted benchmark (details in the lanecard).
- Regression check: Redwood will run a diff on embeddings and top-k outputs for the anchor prompts and provide an SNR score.

Operational responsibilities (owners):
- Redwood (Evelyn / Priyom): provision sandbox, upload assets, provide credentials, run baseline latency benchmark, deliver audit export.
- NovaRetail (Alice / Samir): run acceptance tests, share pass/fail matrix, notify Redwood of extension request.
- Legal (Laura): shepherd MAP signature and confirm NDA appendix.

I’ve updated the attached MAP_NovaRetail_v3.xlsx to include the extension clause and the audit-export deliverable. If that looks good, Laura can route to legal and we’ll kick off provisioning once signed.

On the security point: Karthik has offered to run a short recorded walkthrough of the sandbox controls for your InfoSec team next week. Karthik — can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Evelyn

Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2026 17:09:15 -0800
Subject: Redwood sandbox controls — short checklist

Alice / Samir —

Below is the two-page checklist I promised. (I’ve pasted the highlights here and attached the full checklist to the HubSpot deal folder.)

Highlights:
- Network isolation: sandbox instances run in a customer-specific VPC with no outbound egress except to sanctioned monitoring endpoints.
- Data handling: input payloads are stored in encrypted ephemeral volumes; KV caches are wiped on credential revocation; no training telemetry leaves the sandbox by default.
- Audit logs: redacted CSV export available within 48 hours of request; logs include timestamp, prompt hash, model variant, and token counts.
- Takedown procedure: credentials revoked, S3 objects removed, ephemeral volumes destroyed, cache flush, and a cryptographic checkpoint recorded.

Next steps: I’m available Monday 11/23 10:00–12:00 PT or Tuesday 11/24 14:00–16:00 PT for a 30-minute walkthrough demo. Let me know which slot works and I’ll send an invite.

—Karthik
